question.text: Vaigai Agri Fund (Cat I): Committed INR 60 cr, Hurdle 12% compounded. Compute the incremental HURDLE RETURN accrued IN YEAR 2 only (not cumulative).

explanation.text: **The Logic:** End Year 1 Hurdle NAV = INR 60 x 1.12 = INR 67.20 cr. End Year 2 Hurdle NAV = INR 60 x (1.12)^2 = INR 75.264 cr. Incremental Year-2 hurdle = 75.264 - 67.20 = INR 8.064 crore. (Compound mechanic: Year-2 hurdle is 12% of the prior Hurdle NAV.) **The Trap:** A is simple Year-1 hurdle; C is cumulative 2-year hurdle (15.264); D is simple 12% x 2 years x 60 cr. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C tests compound hurdle across years. Compound vs simple is a common trap. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Compounding matters more for longer-life funds. In a 7-year Infra fund the difference between simple 10% and compound 10% over 7 years is material (70% vs 94.87%) — cite compound in your PPM explicitly and show the multi-year schedule.
